whoami.subject: Moses
clues: I was born to slaves but raised in a palace.
I ran away to the desert and became a shepherd.
God spoke to me from a bush that burned but was not consumed.
I stood before Pharaoh as God sent ten plagues.
I stretched out my hand and parted the Red Sea.

whoami.subject: Noah
clues: God found me righteous in a corrupt generation.
I was given very unusual building instructions.
I built a huge boat out of gopher wood.
I brought the animals aboard two by two.
After my flood, God set a rainbow in the sky.

whoami.subject: David
clues: I was the youngest of eight brothers.
I was a shepherd who played the harp.
I defeated a giant with a sling and a stone.
King Saul grew jealous and chased me.
I became the second king of Israel.

whoami.subject: Jonah
clues: God gave me a job I really did not want.
I tried to sail away from what God told me to do.
A storm hit and I was thrown into the sea.
A great fish swallowed me for three days.
I finally preached to the city of Nineveh.

whoami.subject: Paul
clues: I once persecuted Christians before a big change.
A blinding light stopped me on a road.
I met Jesus on the road to Damascus.
I became a missionary and started many churches.
I wrote many of the letters in the New Testament.

whoami.subject: Peter
clues: I was a fisherman before I followed Jesus.
Jesus said I would become a fisher of men.
I walked on water toward Jesus, then began to sink.
On the night Jesus was arrested, I denied him three times.
I preached at Pentecost and three thousand were saved.

whoami.subject: Abraham
clues: I lived in Ur, but God called me to go to a land I had never seen.
God promised to make me a great nation and bless all the families of the earth through me.
My nephew Lot and I split up because our flocks were too big to share the land.
God told me to count the stars, because that's how many descendants I would have.
I was 100 years old when my son Isaac was born.

whoami.subject: Joseph
clues: I became second in command over all of Egypt.
I was thrown into prison for something I didn't do.
I explained the dreams of Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker.
My jealous brothers sold me to traders headed for Egypt.
My father gave me a beautiful robe of many colors.

whoami.subject: Daniel
clues: I was taken from Jerusalem to Babylon as a young man.
I asked to eat vegetables and drink water instead of the king's food.
I read the mysterious handwriting on the wall.
I kept praying to God three times a day, even when the king made it against the law.
God shut the lions' mouths when I was thrown into their den.

whoami.subject: Esther
clues: I was an orphan raised by my cousin Mordecai.
I was chosen to be queen of Persia.
Wicked Haman plotted to destroy all my people.
I said, "If I perish, I perish," and went to the king without being called.
I risked my life to save the Jews, and they still celebrate Purim.

whoami.subject: Elijah
clues: Ravens brought me bread and meat by a brook.
A widow's flour and oil never ran out while I stayed with her.
I challenged 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel.
God sent fire from heaven to burn up my water-soaked sacrifice.
I went up to heaven in a whirlwind, with chariots of fire.

whoami.subject: Joshua
clues: I was Moses' assistant and went partway up the mountain with him.
I was one of the twelve spies, and only Caleb and I trusted God to give us the land.
I led Israel across the Jordan River on dry ground.
I said, "As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD."
My army marched around Jericho, and the walls fell down.

whoami.subject: Stephen
clues: I was chosen as one of seven men to serve food to the widows.
I was full of grace and power and did great wonders among the people.
False witnesses accused me of speaking against the temple and the Law.
I looked up and saw Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
I was the first Christian martyr, and I prayed for the people stoning me.

whoami.subject: John the Baptist
clues: My father Zechariah couldn't speak until I was named.
I leaped inside my mother when Mary came to visit.
I lived in the wilderness and wore clothes of camel's hair.
I ate locusts and wild honey.
I baptized Jesus in the Jordan River.

whoami.subject: Samson
clues: An angel told my parents I would be a Nazirite from birth.
I tore apart a lion with my bare hands.
I tied torches to the tails of foxes to burn the Philistines' fields.
Delilah tricked me into telling the secret of my strength.
My strength left me when my hair was cut.

whoami.subject: Ruth
clues: I came from the land of Moab.
After my husband died, I refused to leave my mother-in-law, Naomi.
I said, "Where you go I will go, and your people shall be my people."
I gathered leftover grain in the fields of Boaz.
I married Boaz and became the great-grandmother of King David.

memverses.text: You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit. As your fathers did, so do you.
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.
And one called to another and said: “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory!”
since it is written, “You shall be holy, for I am holy.”
“If they sin against you—for there is no one who does not sin—and you are angry with them and give them to an enemy, so that they are carried away captive to the land of the enemy, far off or near,
because, if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
All things were made through him, and without him was not any thing made that was made.
The LORD has established his throne in the heavens, and his kingdom rules over all.
Let no one say when he is tempted, “I am being tempted by God,” for God cannot be tempted with evil, and he himself tempts no one.
Behold, all souls are mine; the soul of the father as well as the soul of the son is mine: the soul who sins shall die.
For by him all things were created, in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities—all things were created through him and for him.
For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh but made alive in the spirit,
For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.
It was to show his righteousness at the present time, so that he might be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus.
for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish.
Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
And this is eternal life, that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.
And by this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments.
You believe that God is one; you do well. Even the demons believe—and shudder!
For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them.

catechism.a: God is the only living and true God. [He’s the all-glorious, almighty, all-knowing, sovereign Creator and Lord of the whole universe. God is perfect and holy, infinite, eternal, and unchanging.]
Nobody made God.

catechism.q: Has God ever had a beginning?
catechism.a: No, God has always been.
No, God lives forever!

catechism.q: Are there more gods than one?
catechism.a: No, there is only one true God.

catechism.q: In how many persons does this one God exist?
catechism.a: God exists in three persons.

catechism.q: Who are the three persons of God?
catechism.a: The three persons of God are the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
God is everywhere.
[No, God is a spirit, and He doesn’t have a body like man.] Though I cannot see God, I know He always sees me.
Yes, God knows all things. [Nothing can be hidden from God.]
Yes, God can do all His holy will.
God made me.
I was made to glorify God and enjoy Him forever.
God made all things.

catechism.q: Why did God make all things?
catechism.a: For His own glory.
I can glorify God by loving Him and doing what He commands.
I should glorify God because He made me and takes care of me.
Adam and Eve were our first parents.

catechism.q: What were Adam and Eve like when God made them?
catechism.a: God made them holy and happy.
No, Adam chose to disobey God.

catechism.q: How did God punish Adam’s disobedience?
catechism.a: Adam’s punishment was death and separation from God.
Sin is disobedience [against God’s perfect law by failing to do what God commands or doing what God forbids.]

catechism.q: What happened to Adam and Eve when they sinned?
catechism.a: Instead of being holy and happy, they became sinful and miserable.

catechism.q: What did Adam’s sin do to you?
catechism.a: It made me guilty and sinful.
The wrath and curse of God.

catechism.q: How sinful are you by nature?
catechism.a: I am corrupt in every part of my being.

catechism.q: Can you go to Heaven with a sinful nature?
catechism.a: No, my heart must be changed before I can go to Heaven.

catechism.q: What is this change of heart called?
catechism.a: Regeneration, being “born again.”

catechism.q: Who can change a sinner’s heart?
catechism.a: Only God can change a sinner’s heart.

catechism.q: Who is the Redeemer of God’s elect?
catechism.a: The only Savior of men is the Lord Jesus Christ, [who being the eternal Son of God, became man and so is both God and man in two natures and one person.]
My heart is changed by the Holy Spirit because of the grace of God.
Grace is God’s kindness to us when we deserve punishment.

catechism.q: What work did Christ do to save you?
catechism.a: Christ perfectly kept the law of God and suffered the punishment due for my sins.

catechism.q: Can anyone be saved by his own works?
catechism.a: No one can be saved by his own works.

catechism.q: What do we gain from the work of Christ?
catechism.a: God regenerates, justifies, and sanctifies those who believe in Christ.
Justification is God forgiving all my sins and declaring me to be righteous.
Sanctification is God making me holy in heart and behavior.

catechism.q: What are the two parts of sanctification?
catechism.a: Dying to sin and living to righteousness.
Whoever repents and believes on the Lord Jesus Christ.

catechism.q: What does it mean to repent?
catechism.a: To repent is to be sorry for sin, and to hate and forsake it [because it displeases God.]
Faith in Christ is trusting in Him alone for salvation.

catechism.q: How were people saved before the coming of Christ?
catechism.a: People were saved by believing in a Savior to come.
No, Jesus lived a sinless life.

catechism.q: What kind of death did Christ die?
catechism.a: A painful and shameful death on the cross.

catechism.q: What are the offices Christ fulfilled as the promised Messiah?
catechism.a: Prophet, Priest, and King.
Christ teaches me the will of God.
Christ died for me; He prays for me, [He washed away my every sin.]
Christ rules over me; He defends me; [He will establish His Kingdom on earth.]

catechism.q: Did Christ remain in the tomb?
catechism.a: No, Christ is risen on the third day, [just as He did say.]
Christ is in heaven, [and He’s praying for me;] He sits at the right hand of God.
Yes, He is coming soon.
No one knows when Christ will return.

catechism.q: What happens to a man when he dies?
catechism.a: The body returns to the dust, and the spirit will go to either heaven or hell.

catechism.q: What will happen when Christ returns?
catechism.a: Our bodies will be raised from the dust, and united again with our spirits.

catechism.q: What will happen to the wicked on Judgment day?
catechism.a: The wicked will go down on judgment day and will be cast into the lake of fire.

catechism.q: What will happen to every Christian on the last day?
catechism.a: Every Christian will live with Jesus in the new heavens and the new earth.

catechism.q: Where do we learn to love and obey God?
catechism.a: In the Bible, we learn to love and obey God.
Holy men of God, who were taught and chosen by God, wrote the Bible.
Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and mind; [and the second is like it, love your neighbor as yourself.]

catechism.q: Of what use are the ten commandments?
catechism.a: They teach us our duty [to God and our duty to man,] and show us our need for a Savior.
Prayer is praising God [for who He is,] thanking God [for what He’s done,] and asking Him for things [He has promised.]

catechism.q: What guide has Christ given to teach us how to pray?
catechism.a: Christ has given us the Lord’s Prayer to teach us how to pray.
